question: What is Merrill's advisor growth strategy, and how has it changed?

claims.text: On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), the CFO said Bank of America continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank (GWIM segment commentary) through its extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors. He said approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors.

At its investor day (deck published 2025-11-05), the GWIM segment listed foundational beliefs that include "having the best advisors enables us to deliver exceptional client outcomes" and "growth of our fully advised client relationships drives financial outcomes". The same deck describes an "industry leading advisor force" of >15K Wealth Advisors across Merrill and the Private Bank combined.

The Merrill Wealth Management page of the November 2025 investor day deck describes a "Leading advisor force", with 95% client satisfaction and "#1 across 9 industry advisor recognition lists in 2025", and gives a footprint of 546 offices in 98 markets.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), the CFO said Merrill FAs see the value of the franchise and "we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors". He added that this "isn't an enormous part of our strategy" and described a training program in wealth management, Bank of America and Merrill as what management believes it can keep driving to improve net new flows.

On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), the CFO said both Merrill and the Private Bank "continued to attract talented advisers who are drawn to the breadth of our platform and our ability to deliver comprehensive solutions". He tied this to the integrated wealth and banking model and said GWIM added 6,000 net new affluent households in the quarter.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CFO said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%. He said the results reflect "our ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform", and that 67% of Merrill clients have banking relationships with the firm. He also said advisor productivity, disciplined pricing, digital engagement and AI tools "continue to expand our capacity to deliver personalized advice at scale".

A Merrill press release (2026-09-15) announced the Tax Efficient Transition Service and Dollar Cost Averaging Service. The head of Managed Account Advisors described them as reflecting a "continued focus on making it easier for advisors to implement personalized investment strategies at scale".

Merrill's recruiting pages (page content as of 2026-11-03) pitch experienced advisors on the brand's 100+ year legacy and on lead-generation infrastructure through Bank of America's global bank and trust division. They also cite access to Merrill's wealth management platform and Bank of America's banking and trust capabilities, and solutions for ultra-high-net-worth clients. The pages say Merrill had 2,112 advisors on Forbes' 2025 "Best-in-State Wealth Advisors" list and 446 on the Forbes 2025 "Top Next-Generation Wealth Advisors Best-in-State" list.

Merrill's Advisor Development Program page (page content as of 2026-11-03) targets entrepreneurial new Financial Advisors. It says roles are designed to help them align banking and investing solutions and build a book of high-net-worth clients.

Over time, the evidence shows the following shift in management's description. In July 2025 the CFO named training and experienced hiring together. In January 2026 he called experienced-advisor recruiting "picking up" but "not an enormous part of our strategy", alongside training. In July and October 2026 he described Merrill and the Private Bank attracting experienced advisers because of the platform's breadth, with AI tools and productivity supporting capacity. These are separate management statements. No source in the evidence describes this as a formal change of strategy.

adjacent.text: GWIM (Merrill plus the Private Bank) 2Q25 net new relationships were 7,100, and about 4.4 trillion dollars of client balances were cited, with strong AUM flows over the past year.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.

adjacent.text: GWIM's 2025 10-K describes Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business as a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets. It reports Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $20.7 billion, up nine percent.
adjacent.differs_because: This describes the client segment and revenue of the business, not an advisor-growth strategy or advisor counts.

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America 10-K/10-Q segment disclosure; investor day materials breaking out Merrill Wealth Management

gaps.what: Merrill-only advisor headcount, experienced-recruit versus trainee mix, and advisor attrition are not disclosed in the evidence. The >15K advisor figure covers Merrill and the Private Bank together.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America earnings supplements or investor day materials with Merrill advisor counts; management commentary on recruiting

gaps.what: No source states that Merrill's advisor growth strategy formally changed. Only the wording across the calls can be compared.
gaps.suggested_source: Management commentary or Q&A from earnings calls and investor day transcripts on recruiting and training priorities
